0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 20 October 1987, after the draft finalized by the Obstetric and Gynaecological Instruments and Appliances CPDC 25, had been Sectional Committee, approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. 0.2 Intra-uterine contraceptive devices ( IUCDs ) present certain unique difficulties for standardization. This Indian Standard defines characteristics of these devices essential to their proper functioning. It describes quantitative physical values, the method of measuring them and the tolerances. 0.3 In the case of IUCDs the very wide variety of shapes, sizes and other properties allow only a general description of their features. 1.1This standard ( Part 1 ) is intended to prescribe general requirements, such as the physical properties, of intra-uterine contraceptive devices, any tails or threads, associated insertion instruments, and for sterilizing, packaging, labelling and -storage of such devices.
1.2 The most important performance criteria have to be assessed by clinical experience and are outside the scope of this standard. 2. DEFINITIONS 2.0 For the purpose of this standard ing definitions shall apply. the follow-

2.3 Visco-Elastic Memory - Property of an intra-uterine contraceptive device which enables it to return approximately to its initial configuration after deformation. 2.4 Tail or Thread - An attachment to an IUCD for the purpose of varifying the presence of an IUCD and enabling the removal of the device which is intended to lie in the cervical canal and the vagina when the body of the IUCD is placed correctly in the uterine cavity. 3. The dimensions of the IUCD ( including any tail or thread ) and its insertion instrument shall be within the tolerances suecified by the manufacturer. 3.4 Composition

its Of which the IUCD, including any tail or thread, and its insertion instrument are made shall be sufficiently resistant to unintended influence by the body fluids and tissues and must be biologically compatible. When identifying plastic materials, IB-spectrophotometry or Differential Scanning Calorimetry ( DSC j or any other appropriate method may be used. 3.5 Visco-Elastic Memory - Those devices which are, by necessity, deformed by the prescribed method of insertion shall have necessary visco-elastic properties to allow them to take up that form in the uterine cavity which is intended by the manufacturer. 3.5.1 Tesr for Vjsco_Elasljc Memory _ The IUCD shall be placed in the insertion system for the maximum time stated in the manufacturer's instructions for insertion. After release it shall rest for 1 minute and then be compared with its original shape.. The deviation shall be within the limits stated by the manufacturer. The test temperature shall be 23 f 2�C. 3.6 Visualization by X-rays - The basic material of the IUCD shall be opaque to X-rays (for example, barium sulphate j. 3.7 Tail or Thread - The tail or thread attached to IUCD to facilitiate its later removal, must be monofilament material which is visually The tai detectable after insertion of the IUCD. or thread and its attachment shall be able to withstand a uniform pull of 12 N for at least 10 seconds. 5.1 The sterile IUCD shall be individually packaged with its insertion instrument. The individual package shall ensure: aj adequate protection of the contents during normal handling, transit and storage; bj maintenance of sterility of the contents under dry, clean and adequately ventilated storage conditions; of the cj Minimal risk for contamination contents during removal from the package; and

5.3 Marking - Each individual package and outer container shall be marked with the following information: a) Brand name of IUCD; b) IUCD size, when appropriate; cj Manufacturer's dj Batch number; ej Month and year of sterilisation; f j Storage directives ( outer container only ); gj The statement `use before............( month and year )`; and specify name and-address;

Insertion instrument should not be re-used." 5.3.1 Standard Marking ~- Each package containing IUCD may also be marked with the Standard Mark. NOTE- The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act.1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an

sterilization procedure ( for example, ethylene oxide, ionising radiation ) shall not have a significant detrimental effect on the properties of the material. Any sterilization should not form toxic substances or detectable impairments of its physical properties ( memory, solidity ). 3.9 Sterility-Where a product is distributed as sterile. it shall be capable of meeting the require-
